transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because... I just can't stop jumping out of my skin lately. I do maintenance work, and if a breaker snaps loudly, or a tool drops on the concrete, or even if somebody just walks up behind me, I practically jump out of my boots. 

And the thing is, it doesn't just stop there. My heart just keeps hammering and hammering in my chest long after everyone else has just moved on and gone back to work. It's getting really hard to deal with.
Did something specific happen to you—like an accident, injury, or traumatic event—before you started noticing these startle reactions and heart pounding?
Yeah, there was. Um... this has all been going on since an arc-flash accident I was in on a retrofit job. It's been about a year and a month now since that happened.
Since the accident, have you been having unwanted memories or flashbacks of what happened during the arc-flash, or nightmares about it?

Yeah, I do. Out of nowhere, I'll just... see that bright flash in my head again. Or I'll hear the trainee who was with me yelling. It happens when I'm not even thinking about it, like if I'm just loading tools into the back of my truck. It just hits me, and it knocks me sideways, honestly. It feels exactly like it's happening all over again. And the nightmares... yeah, those happen too. It's just hard to escape it.
